cells.tense: The thing under your hands is coming to its end, and it is being let come.
cells.act: adjust the share until it is fair, then stop
cells.ask: Look at the ending under your hands and who is carrying what around it — move a part so it sits fairly, then leave it alone.
cells.core:
You can let something finish in the open. You feel what's done and you don't hold it, so the space it leaves gets used, and your sense of the next thing stays a real bearing rather than a wish.

After an ending you have one pull worth guarding: to even out who carried what. Once. Take the thing that's closing and see who was left holding which part; move one piece so the weight squares, then let the rest be. Do it again and the ending turns into a ledger and the bearing goes dim. This isn't indifference — it's settling the account in a single motion and letting the account be settled.
cells.sheetLine: You let a finished thing end, and even the share once.
cells.verb: letting what's finished come to its end so something else can take its place
cells.place: where what you actually want is still just a bearing, not a road

cells.tense: You will end this before it has run, and the next ending is already being chosen.
cells.act: stay in contact while it is hard
cells.ask: Name the next thing you're pulling the plug on — then stay near whoever is most inside it this week, and don't wrap it up for them.
cells.core:
Where you steer by what you want, endings get declared before the thing has lived, and each is spoken of as liberation. Underneath is bracing: get the loss behind you first so it can't be given to you. The clearing stops being something you feel and starts being something you do to whatever might end by itself.

Contact is what reopens this. Take the next ending you were about to announce and stay with the people inside it for a week instead of closing it early. Sit in the middle with them and don't rush them out the other side. A farewell you declared in advance is a flinch wearing its coat; one that comes after you've stayed is finished.
cells.sheetLine: You end things early and name it freedom — the bracing shows.

cells.tense: You were at that ending some time back, and the doorway is where you remain.
cells.ask: Begin a thing you want today without waiting to feel settled — the first move, made now, not the mood around it.
cells.core:
The pull toward what you want is intact. What hasn't moved is the ending that would let you follow it. Something finished is where you left it, and holding it looks like loyalty. The draw toward light stays a bearing instead of a road, and nothing new gets the room.

Direction comes through a step, not through deciding. Pick the smallest move toward something you actually want — a message, a visit, a first piece of the thing you keep describing — and take it today, before you feel certain. One real move does more than a season of holding. The ending doesn't need to be performed. It can just be left where it is, in the rear, while you walk.

cells.tense: Something is ending in you at this moment, and it has not been named or noticed.
cells.act: write the order things go in
cells.ask: Take what's shifting in you and set down the order it goes in — what ends, what stays, what comes after.
cells.core:
You've been steering by a light you hadn't pointed at, and something has been finishing underneath the whole time. Nothing in you has marked it, so the change goes on unnamed, and you describe your direction as a given rather than a choice you keep making.

Put the order down. Take what's shifting and lay out what ends, what stays, what comes after. A scrap of paper will do, or a date and a place attached to it. This doesn't decide anything early or close a door. It lets you see which ending is underway, so your sense of the next thing stops being a hunch and starts being a bearing you chose.

attempts.check: The record does not support any claim about what the person is ending, why, or how long they have held it — the Too Much cell in particular can only show that endings are being reached for ahead of ripening, never name what was ended. A reader could reasonably say 'you don't know what I've been through'; that is fine, because each ask is a self-contained act (a share adjusted, a piece done before readiness) that teaches proportion or forward motion even if the read is wrong. The sentence that serves me more than them is any clause that treats the seat's pull toward light as already arrived; I've kept it as orientation, not attainment, throughout.
